candidate.answerReason: The trip covers 860 miles and uses 32 gallons between full tanks. The quotient 860/32 = 26.875 rounds to 26.9.

methods.label: Track gasoline between full tanks
methods.explanation:
The initial \(6\) gallons fill the tank before the trip begins. The tank is also full after the final refill, so the gasoline added after the initial fill replaces exactly the gasoline used during the trip. Thus the car used
\[
12+20=32\text{ gallons}.
\]
The distance traveled is the difference between the final and initial odometer readings:
\[
57{,}060-56{,}200=860\text{ miles}.
\]
Average miles per gallon means total miles divided by total gallons used, so it is
\[
\frac{860}{32}=26.875.
\]
The hundredths digit is \(7\), so rounding to the nearest tenth gives \(26.9\) miles per gallon, choice D.
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses elementary fuel accounting, division, and decimal rounding, all appropriate for AMC 8.

An arithmetic mean of the two segment efficiencies is unnecessary.
